CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

What You'll Do:

The Corporate Development Associate will support our Equity Capital Markets (ECM) and Investor Relations (IR) efforts as we continue to scale as a public company. This role will be instrumental in executing equity-related capital markets activity, supporting investor engagement, and partnering closely with Finance, Legal, and executive leadership.

The ideal candidate brings strong experience from an investment banking background, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is excited to help build and scale best-in-class capital markets and investor relations processes.

### In this role you will:

- Support CoreWeave’s equity capital markets activities, including public equity offerings, convertibles, and PIPE transactions

- Partner closely with internal stakeholders and external advisors (banks, legal counsel, auditors) throughout equity capital raises

- Support ongoing engagement with sell-side and buy-side analysts, including preparation of key messaging, materials, coordination of meetings, regular direct dialogue, and follow-ups

- Own and manage the corporate access calendar, including investor meetings, conferences, roadshows, and non-deal roadshows

- Play a key role in the quarterly earnings process, including preparation of earnings materials, scripts, Q&A, and coordination across teams

- Assist in the development and refinement of investor-facing materials, including earnings decks, investor presentations, and disclosures

- Help ensure consistency and accuracy of external financial messaging in partnership with Finance, Legal, and Communications

- Track market activity, peer performance, and investor sentiment to help inform leadership and strategy

### Who You Are:

- 2+ years of experience in Capital Markets at an investment bank (ECM, leveraged finance, or closely related role)

- Strong understanding of equity markets, public company processes, and investor dynamics

- Exceptional analytical, organizational, and project management skills

- Ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously in a fast-moving environment

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with comfort interfacing with senior leaders and external stakeholders

- High degree of ownership, attention to detail, and sound judgment

- Experience working with public companies, or supporting IPO-ready organizations, is a plus

Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values: 

- Be Curious at Your Core

- Act Like an Owner

- Empower Employees

- Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences

- Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the organization's growth opportunities are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

The base salary range for this role is $99,000 to $145,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).

## About the Team

We are seeking a subject matter expert (SME) in Data Center Commissioning and Quality. This role requires direct knowledge of data center construction, with a strong focus on MEP systems.

You will work directly with CoreWeave’s project coordination team to make sure projects across the CoreWeave portfolio are completed on time and to the highest quality standards. You will oversee the installation and testing of components and systems, including mission-critical systems such as generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution equipment, and redundancy protocols, as well as cooling systems such as chillers and CDUs.

This is a remote-eligible position with 50% travel required. Candidates must live in or near one of these regions: Northern Virginia; Dallas, Texas; Richmond, Virginia; Livingston, New Jersey; or Atlanta, Georgia.

- Keep safety at the forefront of all construction initiatives.

- Collaborate with general contractors, trade partners, and vendors as needed.

- Serve as a liaison between clients and internal teams, facilitating communication during commissioning activities.

- Help develop, review, and implement commissioning plans as needed.

- Help coordinate and attend pre-construction commissioning meetings.

- Attend construction progress and pre-installation job-site meetings to gather relevant information.

- Review meeting minutes for necessary revisions and help resolve discrepancies related to design intent.

- Inspect field installations, witness functional and commissioning tests, and conduct site visits as needed.

- Travel to sites, client meetings, and training as required.

- Help develop reports for leadership teams and clients on project progress, problems, and solutions.

## Qualifications:

- 5+ years of experience in MEP commissioning, ideally within data centers or critical facilities.

- Understanding of data center systems, BMS/EPMS, and MEP building systems.

- Experience with electrical and low-voltage equipment coordination, and with commissioning or quality assurance.

- Familiarity with relevant design and local codes, as well as industry standards (NEC, NFPA, IEEE, ASHRAE).

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, Outlook).

- Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.

- Strong work ethic, self-motivation, and the assertiveness to keep processes on schedule.

- Ability to maintain relationships with contractors, clients, and internal departments.

- Willingness to travel 50% and respond to after-hours communications in emergencies.

- A valid driver’s license with no significant MVA points or violations.

- Work authorization that does not require company sponsorship now or in the future.

- Experience with commissioning software and tools.

### What You’ll Do:

Our Data Center Operations team is at the physical core of our business, responsible for building, maintaining, and operating the cutting-edge infrastructure that powers the cloud. This team ensures the stability, security, and scalability of our physical assets, working hands-on in a fast-paced, hyper-growth environment. You will join a collaborative and curious group that is essential to delivering a best-in-class experience for our clients.

### About the Role:

As the Data Center Manager, you will be the on-site leader responsible for the operational excellence of our facility. This is a 100% onsite role. Your day-to-day will involve guiding a team of technicians through hardware diagnostics, physical repairs, and new equipment installations while developing and implementing best practices to maximize uptime. You will serve as the key point of contact for all on-site activities, responding to technical emergencies and coordinating with cross-functional teams. This role requires a hands-on approach to leadership, ensuring the reliability and performance of our critical infrastructure.

### In this role, you will:

- Lead a team of data center technicians in daily operations, including server maintenance, equipment installation, and troubleshooting.

- Develop and implement best practices for data center operations to ensure maximum efficiency and uptime.

- Coordinate with cross-functional teams to support client projects and ensure seamless service delivery.

- Perform regular inspections and audits of data center equipment to maintain optimal performance and reliability.

- Respond to and resolve technical issues and emergencies promptly, ensuring minimal downtime and disruption.

- Train and mentor junior technicians to enhance their skills and knowledge of data center operations.

- Collaborate with management to develop and execute strategic initiatives to improve data center performance and scalability.

### Who You Are:

- 5+ years of experience in data center operations, with at least 2+ years in a leadership or supervisory role.

- In-depth knowledge of data center infrastructure, including servers, networking equipment, and cooling systems.

- Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to quickly diagnose and resolve technical issues.

- Experience with data center management tools and software 

- Excellent time management, organization, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead a team

- Proficiency with the Linux Operating System.

- Capable of meeting all physical requirements with reasonable accommodations.

- Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work in elevated locations.

- Flexibility to work in a 24/7 operational environment, participating in on-call rotations, and providing after-hours support.

- Quick decision-making ability and adeptness at task prioritization.

Preferred:

Hands-on OR education-based experience with any of the following areas:

- Computer Hardware, including troubleshooting and repair skills experience

- 5+ years of data center experience

- Computer Networking experience

- Python, Bash, or other scripting languages experience

- Experience with Cisco IOS and/or Juniper JunOS

- Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

- Certifications such as CompTIA Server+, Network+, or equivalent are a plus.

Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.

- You love to lead and mentor a technical team to solve complex infrastructure challenges.

- You’re curious about the latest advancements in data center hardware and infrastructure management.

- You’re an expert in diagnosing and resolving critical hardware and network issues under pressure.

The base salary range for this role is $95,000 to $105,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. us.content:

## What You’ll Do

CoreWeave is seeking a Security Engineer to spearhead the design, deployment, and integration of Wireless Intrusion Detection Systems (WIDS) across our rapidly expanding global physical security network, standardized on the Bastille Networks wireless airspace cybersecurity platform. This role is built for a technical owner with deep expertise in RF spectrum monitoring, wireless threat detection, and the integration of WIDS telemetry into enterprise security platforms. They will lead the charge in detecting rogue access points, rogue cell towers, unauthorized wireless devices, and RF-based threats across our data center estate, and surfacing those events into our centralized security operations.

The ideal candidate brings a blend of sophisticated networking and RF skills, hands-on experience with the Bastille platform and sensor arrays, a mastery of the Genetec Security Center ecosystem, a proven ability to integrate complex third-party systems within Azure or GCP environments, and an understanding of wireless threat detection best practices and how to deploy them at scale. We are looking for a collaborative, customer-centric engineer who pairs technical administration expertise with the ability to produce high-quality technical documentation and results.

This role is based out of any of our hub locations. The position requires up to 20% travel — including international assignments for on-site project execution - and flexibility for after-hours support to ensure the continuous monitoring of our global operations.

## About the Role

- Design, deploy, and maintain the Bastille Networks WIDS platform and sensor arrays across CoreWeave's data center facilities, offices, and PoP sites in support of our Global Security Operations Center (GSOC).

- Architect and implement the integration of Bastille wireless detection telemetry into the Genetec Security Center ecosystem, translating wireless threat events into actionable alarms, events, and event-to-actions within Security Desk via API/SDK, syslog, or middleware as required.

- Deploy and tune Bastille RF spectrum monitoring to detect and localize rogue access points, rogue cell towers, unauthorized wireless devices, Bluetooth/BLE and IoT threats, and other RF-based risks across 50+ wireless protocols.

- Conduct RF site surveys and design sensor placement and coverage plans to ensure accurate device localization across each facility's airspace.

- Support the configuration and hardening of Bastille sensors, concentrators, and supporting server/cloud infrastructure, ensuring alignment with published standards and industry best practices.

- Develop and maintain a comprehensive library of WIDS documentation, including sensor placement plans, RF coverage/heat maps, integration architecture diagrams, and troubleshooting playbooks.

- Create, uphold, and maintain change management processes, ensuring all Bastille configuration and integration changes are meticulously documented, tested, and approved.

- Establish alerting and escalation workflows so GSOC operators receive, triage, and respond to wireless intrusion events through Genetec and unified security tooling.

- Maintain an audit-ready inventory of authorized and unauthorized wireless devices, supporting shadow-IT elimination and regulatory compliance evidence.

- Perform technical root cause analysis for false positives, sensor coverage gaps, and detection failures, implementing corrective actions to improve detection fidelity.

- Collaborate with network, IT security, and SOC teams to correlate Bastille detections with broader wireless security posture, CAASM/XDR/Zero Trust tooling, and threat intelligence.

## Who You Are

- 5+ years of experience in Physical Security Engineering, Network Engineering, wireless/RF security, or a related technical infrastructure role.

- Hands-on experience deploying and operating Wireless Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (WIDS) and RF spectrum monitoring platforms; direct experience with the Bastille Networks platform and sensor arrays strongly preferred.

- Advanced expertise in the Genetec Security Center platform, including Directory, Archiver, and Synergis roles, as well as event-to-action, alarm management, and API/SDK integrations for ingesting third-party telemetry.

- Strong understanding of wireless protocols and standards (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax, Bluetooth/BLE, Zigbee, cellular), RF fundamentals, and common wireless attack vectors (rogue APs, rogue cell towers, evil-twin, deauthentication, wireless exfiltration).

- Strong knowledge of Windows Server environments, including deployment, maintenance, and system hardening.

- Solid understanding of networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, routing, VLANs) and SQL databases, including data integrity management and troubleshooting.

- Proven experience integrating third-party systems and deploying field solutions in collaboration with external vendors.

- Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, with strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical field.

- Demonstrated ability to work independently with strong attention to detail and follow-through.

Preferred

- Certifications: GSEC, Security+, Network+, CCNA, CWNA/CWSP (Certified Wireless Security Professional), CISSP, or manufacturer certifications (Bastille, Genetec, Axis, Hanwha, Bosch).

- Specialized Experience: Prior Bastille deployment or administration experience; experience deploying WIDS in enterprise or AI/data center environments, performing RF site surveys, and integrating wireless detection telemetry into a PSIM, SIEM, or Genetec Security Center.

- Industry Context: Familiarity with wireless security controls for data center physical security, Bastille integrations with platforms such as Axis, Splunk, Cisco, and Lenel, and relevant compliance frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC2).

us.content:

## About the Team

Our Data Center Operations team is at the physical core of our business, responsible for building, maintaining, and operating the infrastructure that powers the cloud. We are seeking Data Center Technicians across a range of experience levels to ensure service availability, physical reliability, and operational excellence across our facilities.

In this salaried, 100% on-site position, you will perform hands-on hardware and network diagnostics, equipment installations, structured cabling, and physical repairs. Your responsibilities and level of autonomy will match your experience, with opportunities to build technical skills and take on more complex work. Candidates will be leveled during the interview process based on technical expertise, depth of experience, and problem-solving ability.

This role requires participation in a rotating on-call schedule. You must live within 60 minutes of the site to support on-call responsibilities and be able to travel up to 15% to other data center locations as needed.

## Key Responsibilities:

- Data Center Operations & Maintenance: Assemble, rack, stack, and maintain data center server, storage, and networking hardware. Maintain hot/cold aisle containment, conduct inventory audits, and perform routine physical maintenance.

- Diagnostics & Repair: Conduct hardware and network diagnostics on live and offline systems. Troubleshoot issues reported through tickets, replace components, and perform physical repairs.

- Equipment Deployment: Support equipment installations, device provisioning, and operating system installations, taking on more complex troubleshooting and deployment work as your experience grows.

- Structured Cabling & Security: Maintain high standards of cable management and structured cabling, and follow physical and cybersecurity protocols.

- Process & Documentation: Maintain accurate inventory records and ticket updates. Contribute to standard operating procedures (SOPs), technical documentation, and process improvements.

- Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing: Collaborate with local and cross-functional teams to support operational readiness. Share knowledge and contribute to team training and development.

- On-Call & Response: Participate in a rotating on-call schedule and be available to arrive on-site within 60 minutes when an incident requires hands-on support.

## Qualifications:

- Hardware Foundation: Hands-on experience or coursework in computer hardware assembly, installation, and physical and logical troubleshooting.

- Operating Systems & Networking: Familiarity with Linux operating systems and fundamental networking concepts.

- Problem-Solving & Judgment: Ability to follow established procedures, prioritize tasks, troubleshoot technical issues, and recognize when to ask for guidance or escalate.

- Communication & Teamwork: Strong organizational and communication skills, a collaborative and curious mindset, and a commitment to high reliability standards.

- Learning & Development: Willingness to build technical skills, learn new systems, and take on responsibilities that match your experience.

- Physical Requirements: Ability to perform the following essential duties, with or without reasonable accommodation:

- Move and position equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.

- Remain in a stationary position for extended periods while performing diagnostics and repairs.

- Access equipment in confined spaces, under-floor areas, and on ladders.

- Handle small hardware components, connectors, and cabling with precision.

- Work in data center environments with hot/cold aisle temperatures ranging from 60°F to 90°F.

### Preferred Skills:

- Associate’s degree, bachelor’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Networking, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience in enterprise or commercial data center environments.

- Experience with Linux OS administration, command-line tools, and device provisioning.

- Scripting and automation experience with Python, Bash, or shell scripts.

- Networking experience with Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, or enterprise switch/router configurations.

- Industry certifications such as CompTIA A+, Network+, Server+, or Linux+.

- Data Center Operations & Maintenance: Assemble, rack, stack, and maintain data center server, storage, and networking hardware. Maintain hot/cold aisle containment, conduct inventory audits, and perform routine physical maintenance.

- Diagnostics & Repair: Conduct hardware and network diagnostics on live and offline systems. Troubleshoot issues reported through tickets, replace components, and perform physical repairs.

- Equipment Deployment: Support equipment installations, device provisioning, and operating system installations, taking on more complex troubleshooting and deployment work as your experience grows.

- Structured Cabling & Security: Maintain high standards of cable management and structured cabling, and follow physical and cybersecurity protocols.

- Hardware Foundation: Hands-on experience or coursework in computer hardware assembly, installation, and physical and logical troubleshooting.

- Operating Systems & Networking: Familiarity with Linux operating systems and fundamental networking concepts.

- Learning & Development: Willingness to build technical skills, learn new systems, and take on responsibilities that match your experience.

- Physical Requirements: Ability to perform the following essential duties, with or without reasonable accommodation:

- Move and position equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.

- Remain in a stationary position for extended periods while performing diagnostics and repairs.

- Access equipment in confined spaces, under-floor areas, and on ladders.

- Handle small hardware components, connectors, and cabling with precision.

- Work in data center environments with hot/cold aisle temperatures ranging from 60°F to 90°F.

### Preferred Skills:

- Associate’s degree, bachelor’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Networking, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience in enterprise or commercial data center environments.

- Experience with Linux OS administration, command-line tools, and device provisioning.

- Scripting and automation experience with Python, Bash, or shell scripts.

- Networking experience with Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, or enterprise switch/router configurations.

us.content:

Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

## About the Team

The Data Center Design team manages the delivery of comprehensive site, campus, architectural, and engineering designs across CoreWeave’s global data center portfolio. The team’s work covers the full physical planning and development of data center sites, from initial site programming and master planning through the coordinated design of single-building facilities and large-scale, multi-building campuses. This includes establishing the overall layout, building locations and orientations, land utilization, construction and capacity phasing, central plants, site access and circulation, logistics areas, stormwater management, civil works, and provisions for future expansion.

The Data Center Engineering team creates an integrated design that coordinates each data center building with power, cooling, water, telecommunications, controls, life-safety, security, and other shared infrastructure systems. The team is also responsible for the comprehensive design of the buildings and their supporting systems and equipment, including architecture, structure, building envelope, mechanical systems, electrical infrastructure, plumbing, controls, fire protection, and life-safety systems. The team coordinates the full design lifecycle from early-stage site planning and project definition through detailed design, construction, commissioning support, and IT deployment. It makes sure CoreWeave’s technical requirements are built into each project and delivered in line with established scope, schedule, budget, quality, reliability, scalability, and operational expectations. Through disciplined leadership, multidisciplinary design coordination, and consistent execution, the team enables CoreWeave to rapidly and reliably expand its physical infrastructure to support next-generation, high-density compute workloads.

We are seeking an accomplished and experienced Director of Data Center Engineering to lead CoreWeave’s multidisciplinary team of engineering subject matter experts and set the technical direction for our global data center portfolio. This person will develop, maintain, and govern CoreWeave’s Basis of Design, reference designs, engineering standards, and long-term design roadmap for future data centers. As a senior leader within the Data Center Design organization, the Director will serve as the senior technical authority and escalation point for engineering decisions. They will partner with the VP of Design and cross-functional teams, including Design Management, Data Center Technology, Capacity, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, Network Engineering, and Supply Chain, to turn business and technology requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions.

This role requires 20% travel to various data center sites.

## Key Responsibilities:

- Engineering Team Leadership & Development: Lead, manage, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of engineering subject matter experts across mechanical, electrical, plumbing, architectural, civil, structural, controls, and other critical infrastructure disciplines. Establish clear expectations, foster accountability, and support the professional growth of the engineering team.

- Technical Strategy & Direction: Establish the technical vision and engineering strategy for CoreWeave’s global data center portfolio, ensuring infrastructure solutions align with business objectives, customer requirements, deployment timelines, and the evolving needs of high-density AI compute.

- Basis of Design Governance: Lead the development, maintenance, and governance of CoreWeave’s Basis of Design. Ensure requirements are technically sound, clearly documented, consistently interpreted, and updated to reflect lessons learned, operational feedback, technology advancements, and changing business needs.

- Engineering Design Roadmap: Develop and maintain a long-term design roadmap for future data centers, identifying the infrastructure architectures, capacity requirements, technologies, and engineering capabilities needed to support emerging compute platforms and increasing rack densities.

- Multidisciplinary Engineering Integration: Ensure mechanical, electrical, architectural, civil, structural, controls, life-safety, and other engineering disciplines are coordinated into cohesive infrastructure solutions. Partner with Data Center Technology to integrate low-voltage, structured cabling, network, and white space technology requirements.

- Partnership with Design Management: Work closely with Data Center Design Management to define technical requirements, establish design review milestones, resolve engineering issues, evaluate proposed changes, and support timely delivery of coordinated, constructible design packages.

- Design Reviews & Technical Assurance: Set expectations for technical design reviews and lead evaluations of critical drawings, specifications, calculations, equipment selections, control sequences, studies, and commissioning documentation. Ensure design risks, gaps, and interdisciplinary conflicts are identified and resolved.

- Technical Decision-Making & Escalation: Serve as the senior escalation point for complex engineering challenges and decisions. Facilitate alignment among internal subject matter experts and give the VP of Design and executive leadership clear options, risk assessments, and recommendations.

- Infrastructure Performance & Operational Feedback: Collaborate with Operations and Commissioning to review system performance, reliability events, commissioning findings, capacity limitations, and operational trends. Translate findings into corrective actions and improvements to standards, reference designs, and future project requirements.

- Continuous Improvement & Lessons Learned: Establish a structured process for capturing lessons learned from design, construction, commissioning, and operations. Ensure validated improvements are incorporated into the Basis of Design, reference designs, specifications, and engineering processes.

- Innovation & Technology Evaluation: Lead the technical evaluation of emerging data center technologies, including advanced cooling, liquid cooling, power distribution, energy storage, controls, modular infrastructure, and other systems supporting high-density compute. Develop recommendations for testing, standardization, and deployment at scale.

- Reliability, Efficiency & Sustainability: Drive engineering initiatives that improve infrastructure reliability, energy and water efficiency, sustainability, scalability, maintainability, and total cost of ownership without compromising performance or deployment speed.

- Codes, Standards & Compliance: Ensure engineering requirements and designs comply with applicable codes, regulations, safety requirements, contractual obligations, and recognized industry standards. Stay aware of regulatory and technical changes that could affect CoreWeave’s portfolio.

- External Partner & Supplier Engagement: Provide technical direction to data center providers, A/E consultants, contractors, equipment manufacturers, and technology partners. Set clear engineering expectations and evaluate proposed solutions for compliance with CoreWeave’s requirements.

- Equipment Strategy & Standardization: Collaborate with Supply Chain and Construction to define technical requirements for major infrastructure equipment, evaluate vendor solutions, support product qualification, and identify opportunities for standardization and strategic procurement.

- Engineering Resource Planning: Manage engineering resources across the project portfolio, balancing project demands, standards development, technical initiatives, and operational support. Identify capability gaps and develop hiring, consultant, or vendor strategies.

- Executive & Portfolio Reporting: Give the VP of Design and executive leadership clear reporting on engineering priorities, technical risks, major decisions, roadmap progress, resource needs, and initiatives affecting portfolio performance.

- Culture of Technical Excellence: Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, technical rigor, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement within the engineering team. Encourage subject matter experts to challenge assumptions, develop scalable solutions, and maintain a high standard of engineering quality.

## Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering field.

- 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in data center engineering, infrastructure design, construction, commissioning, or operations, including at least 8 years in an engineering leadership or people-management role.

- Demonstrated experience leading, developing, and coordinating multidisciplinary teams of technical engineers and subject matter experts across mechanical, electrical, civil, structural, architectural, plumbing, controls, fire protection, and life-safety disciplines.

- Recognized technical expertise in planning and engineering large-scale, high-density data centers, including greenfield developments, single-building facilities, and multi-building campuses.

- Proven experience developing, maintaining, and governing Basis of Design documents, reference designs, technical standards, engineering specifications, and long-term infrastructure design roadmaps.

- Strong knowledge of critical data center infrastructure, including utility services, medium- and low-voltage power distribution, substations, UPS systems, generators, cooling plants, liquid-cooling systems, water systems, BMS and controls, fire protection, and life-safety systems.

- Proven ability to evaluate complex engineering challenges, reconcile competing technical requirements, and make clear, risk-informed decisions that balance reliability, scalability, efficiency, constructability, maintainability, cost, and speed to market.

- Experience providing technical oversight across multiple concurrent projects, locations, delivery models, and stages of development, from early feasibility and master planning through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and operational turnover.

- Experience leading multidisciplinary technical reviews of engineering calculations, studies, drawings, specifications, equipment selections, sequences of operation, commissioning plans, and proposed deviations from established standards.

- Experience working with data center providers, developers, utility companies, A/E consultants, contractors, commissioning agents, equipment manufacturers, and technology partners.

- Strong understanding of applicable building codes, engineering standards, regulatory requirements, safety requirements, and industry best practices for mission-critical facilities.

- Excellent people-leadership skills, including the ability to establish technical accountability, manage performance, develop engineering talent, encourage knowledge sharing, and build a collaborative, high-performing team of subject matter experts.

- Excellent written, verbal, and executive-level communication skills, with the ability to translate complex engineering issues into clear business impacts, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.

- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while balancing technical initiatives, project demands, competing priorities, and evolving infrastructure requirements.

- Strong analytical, strategic-thinking, organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.

### Preferred Skills:

- Advanced degree in engineering or a related field.

- Professional Engineer (PE) licensure, or certifications such as LEED, Uptime Institute, or similar industry qualifications.

- Demonstrated ability to identify, evaluate, and implement emerging data center technologies, particularly for high-density compute, advanced cooling, liquid cooling, power distribution, controls, modular infrastructure, and energy efficiency.

- Ability to keep a portfolio-level perspective while engaging directly in the details needed to resolve critical project issues.

- Ability to bring structure to ambiguity and translate technical and business requirements into actionable project plans.

- Ability to identify developing risks early, set practical mitigation strategies, and communicate recommendations confidently to senior and executive leadership.

- Track record of building productive relationships among internal teams, data center providers, A/E firms, contractors, consultants, and equipment suppliers.

Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About the Team

The Product Security team at CoreWeave is responsible for making sure everything we ship, and everything we use to build it, is secure by design. The team owns application security, vulnerability management, offensive security, AI product security, and product vulnerability response across CoreWeave. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and the rest of Security Foundations. CoreWeave is the essential cloud for AI. Come help us secure the platform the frontier runs on.

CoreWeave is seeking a Director of Product Security to lead this organization. This is a highly technical leadership role. We are building security that runs at machine speed: every change threat modeled at design time, reviewed before it merges, and attacked by our own agents before an adversary gets the chance. What our agents find, our agents fix. Threat models arrive in minutes. Pentesting stops being a queue: agents cover the breadth around the clock, third party firms add depth, and our internal team goes after the hardest targets. Humans set policy and make the consequential calls. Security is one of the reasons customers pick CoreWeave, and this org is a big part of how we earn it.

We are agentic first because the surface is growing faster than any team we could hire, and we expect this leader to build the systems that make that real. You will own the strategy and roadmap for product security across the company, lead the managers and senior engineers who run AppSec, vulnerability management, and offensive security, and build the capabilities we don't have yet. You will also set the bar for how security shows up for CoreWeave engineers: a paved road instead of a toll booth, a product they want to use rather than a tax they have to pay.

Key Responsibilities:

- Define and drive the strategy and roadmap for Product Security at CoreWeave, spanning application security, vulnerability management, offensive security, AI product security, and product vulnerability response.

- Lead and grow a multi-team organization of managers and senior ICs, including hiring the engineering managers who will run each function.

- Build an agentic-first vulnerability program where agents discover, triage, and remediate issues at scale, with the goal of retiring entire classes of risk rather than closing tickets one at a time.

- Own vulnerability management end to end across CoreWeave's infrastructure and products: discovery, prioritization, SLAs, remediation, and reporting to executive leadership.

- Run a tiered offensive security program that combines continuous agentic testing, third party assessments, an internal team focused on our hardest targets, and external researchers through our vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty programs. Adversarial testing of our models, agents, and inference stack is part of the job, built for how AI fails: prompt injection, poisoned tools, and abuse of autonomy.

- Bring offensive security to bear on tenant isolation across shared GPUs, bare metal, and Kubernetes. Platform Security owns the isolation controls and strategy; Product Security makes sure they hold.

- Build the paved road for CoreWeave engineers: secure defaults, controls built into the tools engineers already use, and findings that arrive validated with the fix attached.

- Establish one secure development lifecycle for the whole business, including threat modeling, secure design review, and security tooling in CI/CD, and extend it to companies we acquire.

- Own security for CoreWeave's AI products and for the AI tooling our engineers build with, including model and dataset supply chain, agent tooling, and the provenance of AI-generated code.

- Stand up and run product vulnerability response (PSIRT): intake, coordinated disclosure, customer communication, and fixes across the product portfolio.

- Embed Product Security Partners in critical product areas with authority to make design-time security decisions within policy, and maintain a standing leadership cadence with Product Management.

- Partner with Cloud Security, Platform Security, Detection and Response, and GRC to keep the prevent, detect, and respond boundaries clear and the handoffs clean.

Qualifications:

- 10+ years in security or software engineering, with significant time in application security, vulnerability management, or offensive security.

- 5+ years of security leadership experience, including managing managers and scaling a multi-team organization.

- Proven track record of building or running a product security program at a cloud provider, security company, or large-scale SaaS business.

- Experience taking over existing teams and integrating them into one organization. Most of this org exists today, and you will inherit it.

- A track record of moving engineering leaders on architecture and roadmap decisions you don't own.

- A strong bias for action. You're scrappy, you move fast, and you own the outcome, including the parts nobody assigned to you.

- Hands-on depth in modern application security. You can read a threat model, review a fix, and tell a real finding from noise.

- Experience operating a vulnerability management program at scale, including metrics, SLAs, and executive reporting, and strong opinions about how to do it well.

- Direct experience with offensive security, either running a red team or penetration testing program or having done the work yourself.

- Working knowledge of how AI systems are built and deployed, and of the new security problems that come with LLMs, agents, and model supply chains.

- Enough familiarity with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and CI/CD to be credible with the engineers who build them.

- Experience building and mentoring diverse, inclusive, high-performing teams in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Skills:

- Experience deploying AI agents or LLM-based tooling for security work, or building the platform they run on.

- Experience running a PSIRT or coordinated vulnerability disclosure function.

- Experience with the security side of M&A diligence and integration.

- Public contributions to the security community: open source, research, talks, or CVEs.

Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk:

- You think security should feel like a product engineers want to use, and you measure yourself by whether they actually use it.

- You'd rather eliminate a class of vulnerabilities than get very good at fixing them one at a time.

- You're comfortable leading through ambiguity and change, and you can balance long-term platform investments with the finding that needs fixing today.

- You have a strong owner's mindset and you stay technical. You still read code, findings, and pentest reports.

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. ## About the Role:

CoreWeave is seeking a GSOC Operator to join our 24/7/365 team in Livingston, NJ. This role supports the protection of CoreWeave personnel and infrastructure, corporate offices, data centers, other monitored locations, and the physical security systems that support those environments.

GSOC Operators continuously monitor physical security and situational-awareness systems; assess, document, and coordinate response to physical security, life safety, cyber-physical, and monitoring-degradation events; execute approved access and credential workflows; and serve as a central communications hub for internal teams, onsite security, service providers, emergency responders, and other authorized stakeholders.

This role includes monitoring our wireless intrusion detection system capabilities

Operational Notice: This is a 24/7 on-site team. You will be required to commit to rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays, to ensure continuous operational coverage.

## What You’ll Do:

### Security Monitoring & System Health

- Conduct proactive, continuous monitoring and operational checks of Genetec Security Center, CCTV, access control, intrusion detection, alarm, environmental and life-safety notification, and related physical security systems.

- Assess and validate alarms using available video, access-control, site, and contextual information; perform approved first-line troubleshooting; and escalate system faults or monitoring degradation to the responsible engineering, network, facilities, provider, or site team.

- Document, route, track, and escalate physical-security system issues and related work items through resolution, including coordinating technician access and confirming restoration of monitoring capability.

### Access & Credential Operations

- Process approved physical-access and credential requests, perform required identity-verification steps, and produce, quality-check, package, ship, track, secure, suspend, or deactivate credentials in accordance with established procedures and authorization requirements.

- Conduct authorized after-hours virtual escorts and maintain continuous monitoring, communication, and documentation for the duration of each escort.

### Incident Management & Emergency Response

- Serve as the initial intake and coordination point for physical-security, life-safety, cyber-physical, and monitoring-degradation events; assess available information and initiate required response actions without unnecessary delay.

- Create and maintain incident records in Ontic, assign initial GSOC severity, and initiate approved PagerDuty and private /inci escalation workflows when required.

- Coordinate the physical-security component of active incidents, including onsite response, CCTV review, access-control correlation, evidence preservation, factual status updates, and documented transfer of incident ownership when another function assumes the lead.

- Initiate and support post-incident reviews for qualifying events by preserving evidence, reconstructing timelines, documenting lessons learned, and tracking follow-up actions.

- Maintain accurate shift-log entries and complete structured written and verbal handovers of open incidents, access requests, monitoring degradation, and other unresolved operational items.

### Communication, Intelligence & Documentation

- Serve as a central communications hub, providing clear, timely, and factual updates through approved channels to CoreWeave teams, onsite security, service providers, emergency responders, and other authorized stakeholders.

- Operate Wave PTX Dispatch to monitor, acknowledge, and coordinate radio communications using assigned call signs, plain language, and closed-loop communication.

- Monitor threat, weather, provider, and other situational-awareness sources; assess potential impact to CoreWeave people and locations; and prepare approved advisories, BOLOs, SITREPs, or other internal products.

- Execute authorized Everbridge notifications and monitor delivery, acknowledgements, assistance requests, and emergency-accountability activity.

- Maintain accurate, contemporaneous records in Ontic and the designated shift log; use Jira and other approved systems for access and service-request workflows.

- Produce clear, timely incident summaries, timelines, evidence references, and approved reports for authorized stakeholders.

Note: Duties and responsibilities outlined are subject to change and refinement based on evolving operational demands.

## Who You Are:

- Experience: 2+ years of experience in GSOC/PSOC environments, dispatch center, emergency operations center, data center security operations, critical-infrastructure monitoring environment, or related role.

- Technical Skills: Working knowledge of CCTV, access control, intrusion detection, alarm monitoring, incident management, and emergency communications systems; experience with Genetec Security Center or a comparable platform.

- Tools: Experience with incident management and collaboration platforms such as Ontic, Jira, Slack, Google Workspace, or comparable systems.

- Operational Capability: Demonstrated ability to assess risk, prioritize competing events, make timely decisions within defined authority, escalate appropriately, and coordinate response under pressure.

- Vigilance: Ability to maintain sustained vigilance, manage multiple systems and communications channels, and accurately assess CCTV, access-control, alarm, and incident information.

- Communication & Ethics: Proven ability to communicate clearly and professionally under pressure while protecting sensitive and confidential information.

### Preferred:

- Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Information Technology, Criminal Justice, Emergency Management, or equivalent industry experience.

- DHS Incident Command System (ICS) training (ICS-100, ICS-200).

- Genetec certification, ASIS PSP, CPP, or related security certifications and training.

- Experience within data center environments, corporate security, emergency operations, public-safety dispatch, or other critical-infrastructure environments.

- Familiarity with on-call alerting, mass notification, radio dispatch, credentialing, biometric access control, key management, or related security platforms; experience with PagerDuty, Everbridge, Wave PTX, HID Origo, ClearID, Alcatraz, BioConnect, or comparable systems is a plus.

- Exposure to wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS) and broader RF threats, including unauthorized-device investigations; Bastille Wireless Airspace Cybersecurity Platform experience is preferred.

Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk. 

- You love to solve complex security challenges and protect critical infrastructure.

- You’re curious about learning and mastering new security technologies and systems.

- You maintain focus, sound judgment, and composure during high-stress or rapidly changing incidents.

## Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

About the Team

CoreWeave's Global Tax team is an AI native tax team; we are builders at our core. The team supports one of the fastest-scaling infrastructure footprints in the AI industry. We manage tax across roughly 50 data center sites in the United States and an asset base of approximately $22 billion of equipment, hardware, and GPUs — a base that is forecast to more than double again over the next two years. Our Indirect Tax function owns sales and use tax, property tax, business licenses, gross receipts taxes, and the exemption and incentive strategies that make a buildout of this scale economical.

Key Responsibilities:
This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to own the direct and indirect taxation of fixed assets at a company adding sites faster than most operators add racks. You are a builder and will bring a forward thinking mindset on how to incorporate AI into everyday tasks to improve and develop the workflows that you own. You will run the US property tax cycle, maintain the tax fixed asset data that drives depreciation and property tax reporting, and be the day-to-day point of contact for our outside property tax advisors. You will support the self-development buildout on construction-period questions and equipment exemptions, and work with Direct Tax on the depreciation inputs that flow into the provision and tax return. There is a clear path here to owning the function outright as the footprint grows.

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Global Tax & Innovation, the Manager, Tax Infrastructure will manage the tax reporting and compliance obligations attached to CoreWeave's physical asset base — property tax, tax fixed asset data, and the exemption positions that follow equipment from purchase order through placed-in-service. This role sits at the seam between direct and indirect tax, and partners closely with Tax Operations, Accounting Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Data Center Construction.

In this role, you will:

- Manage the US property tax compliance cycle — filings, assessment review, bill processing, payment approval, accruals, and appeal support — across a rapidly expanding set of sites and taxing jurisdictions.

- Maintain the tax fixed asset data set: reconcile it to the NetSuite asset register and the capital forecast, resolve asset classification and location discrepancies, and prepare the data that supports tax depreciation and property tax reporting.

- Work side by side with Accounting Operations to build a deep working understanding of the fixed asset lifecycle — from purchase order and receipt, through construction-in-progress, capitalization and in-service dating, to inter-site transfers, disposals and retirements — and know what each stage means for property tax reporting and tax depreciation.

- Prepare and update the property tax forecast each quarter, including identifying new locations against each lien date and reflecting construction-in-progress and inventory positions.

- Manage property tax audits and assessment appeals day to day: assemble the asset records auditors request, prepare the valuation and classification support, and act as a direct point of contact for assessors and auditors rather than routing everything through an advisor.

- Serve as the day-to-day contact for outside property tax advisors: manage the calendar, supply clean reconciled data rather than raw extracts, review deliverables, and track fees against scope so advisor spend grows more slowly than the asset base.

- Support Supply Chain, Procurement, and Logistics on the tax consequences of asset movement — receipt location versus use location, third-party logistics receiving models, and exemption certificate and direct pay permit administration.

- Support Data Center Construction and Site Development on self-developed sites, including construction-period questions, sales and use tax on construction inputs versus operating equipment, and construction pay application review — building direct working relationships with those teams rather than working through intermediaries.

- Partner with Direct Tax to deliver fixed asset inputs needed for determination of depreciation methods analysis, placed-in-service determinations, and tax reporting.

- Track capital investment and abatement commitments tied to incentive agreements and prepare the supporting documentation.

- Document and improve the processes and controls behind all of the above so they scale with capital expenditure volume.

Qualifications: 

- 6+ years of progressive tax experience, including time in-house or in a service capacity for capital-intensive businesses — data center, cloud, telecommunications, energy, manufacturing, or real estate.

- Hands-on experience preparing or managing US property tax compliance, including real and personal property filings, assessment review, and accrual support.

- Direct experience working in a tax fixed asset register — reconciling asset data, resolving classification and location issues, and producing depreciation reporting from it.

- Working knowledge of federal tax depreciation mechanics, including MACRS, bonus depreciation, and placed-in-service determinations.

- Experience applying sales and use tax to capital equipment, including exemption certificate management and equipment taxability analysis.

- Experience working directly with Accounting Operations and with Supply Chain or Procurement — you can trace an asset from purchase order to receipt to capitalization to return.

- Proficiency with ERP and fixed asset systems (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle Fixed Assets, or comparable) and advanced Excel; comfort working with large data sets.

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Preferred:

- Progress toward or completion of a CPA or CMI (Property Tax) designation.

- Data center construction or development experience, including exposure to construction-in-progress and construction pay applications.

- Cost segregation experience, or experience supporting asset classification studies.

- Exposure to state and local incentives and abatement compliance reporting.

- Exposure to tax technology and automation and genuine interest in using AI tooling to compress compliance cycles.

This is not a role where you wait to be asked, you bring a clear point of view, operate independently across complex situations, and are embedded deeply enough in the business to anticipate what leaders need before they articulate it.

You think about the upstream and downstream implications of every recommendation, build trusted relationships through coaching and knowledge sharing, and consistently deliver high-quality outcomes even in ambiguous or fast-moving environments. This person shapes initiatives, refines how people work gets done across Data Center Operations, and elevates the quality of decisions across the organization.

Success in this role means turning priorities into practical, scalable solutions that help the organization operate effectively, and leaving the function better than you found it.

What You’ll Do:

As a People Business Partner for Data Center Operations, you'll be the strategic and operational backbone for people decisions across CoreWeave's data center footprint. You'll enable leaders to move fast without sacrificing judgment, turning ambiguous, high-stakes people challenges into clear, defensible decisions that support execution and growth.

You'll own core people processes end-to-end, balancing executional rigor with speed. You'll spot patterns before they become problems, surface insights leaders haven't asked for yet, and step in early enough to course-correct before challenges impact delivery. This role exists to reduce friction, increase clarity, and amplify leadership impact as the organization scales.

Your impact will be felt across various dimensions:

- Strategic Partnership: Serve as an influential thought partner to Data Center Operations leaders, helping translate business goals into people decisions that improve execution, support growth, and strengthen organizational effectiveness. Anticipate how priorities are evolving and align your work accordingly, before leaders come to you with the problem.

- Execute with Impact: Consistently deliver high-quality outcomes across complex, often ambiguous workstreams. Balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, stepping into the details when needed and knowing when to pull back. Consider the upstream and downstream implications of decisions before recommending a path.

- Pattern Recognition & Insights: Leverage data, observations, and deep domain expertise to identify recurring patterns across Data Center Operations, surfacing signals proactively, synthesizing them into clear actions, and helping leaders course-correct before challenges compound.

- Enable Change at Speed: Lead organizational change in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, ensuring seamless transitions, transparency, and business continuity. As a People Business Partner, you're driving change, not just managing through it. Able to execute at speed without sacrificing quality of work.

- Talent Management: Drive workforce planning, talent calibration, and performance management activities across Data Center Operations, enabling consistent and defensible people decisions. Apply deep expertise to hold the bar on job architecture and leveling in a function where those lines can blur.

- People Risk & Workplace Advisory: Independently manage complex people matters, balancing risk, speed, and business practicality with sound judgment. Owning the resolution, not just the escalation.

- Meet the Business Where It Lives: You're willing and able to travel regularly to data center sites (30% travel) and are comfortable building credibility with frontline teams, not just senior leaders. You see time on-site as core to doing the job well, not a disruption to it, and you understand that operations environments run differently than corporate ones,  adapting your communication style, cadence, and tools to fit the reality of the teams you support.

- Hold the Line with Judgment: You know when to enforce consistency and when to flex, and you can defend either call with sound reasoning. You're comfortable being the person who says "no" or "not yet" when it's the right call for the business, even when it's not the easy answer.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role. You will serve as the subject matter expert for benefits and leave operations in the region and the primary contact for our leave, benefits, and COBRA vendors. Total Rewards owns benefits strategy and plan design; you own how those plans and policies are executed.

- 

Own new-hire and life-event enrollments, eligibility, qualifying-event reviews, dependent verification, and open enrollment execution, maintaining clean data in Workday and at every carrier.

- 

Monitor carrier and vendor EDI feeds and reconcile discrepancies before they reach employees.

- 

Partner with Payroll on deductions, imputed income, and arrears so pay and coverage match.

### Leave of absence and accommodations

- 

Administer the full US leave lifecycle, including FMLA eligibility and designation, state PFML and disability programs, STD and LTD coordination, USERRA, intermittent leave tracking, benefits continuation during leave, and return to work.

- 

Run the accommodation interactive process under the ADA and PWFA, including intake, documentation requests, partnering with managers and PBPs on options, documenting decisions, and keeping medical information confidential and separate from personnel files.

### Canada benefits and leave

- 

Administer group benefits enrollment and changes, EI leave coordination, employer top-ups, Records of Employment, and provincial employment standards leaves.

- 

Apply the duty to accommodate under provincial human rights law, to the point of undue hardship.

### Vendors and compliance

- 

Manage day-to-day relationships with the leave and disability TPA, COBRA administrator, broker, and carriers; hold them to SLAs, escalate errors, and bring vendor performance data to Total Rewards.

- 

Support compliance cycles, including ACA reporting, COBRA and required benefits notices, Form 5500 data requests, and audit-ready leave and accommodation documentation.

- 

Support federal contractor obligations, including Section 503 and VEVRAA requirements.

### Inquiries, playbooks, and continuous improvement

- 

Resolve Tier 2 and Tier 3 benefits, leave, and accommodation inquiries, escalating to Legal or Total Rewards when appropriate.

- 

Build and maintain leave and accommodation playbooks, including state and provincial leave matrices, manager guidance, and templated notices.

- 

Coach People Operations Specialists on benefits and leave questions.

- 

Identify and reduce manual work and friction, such as improving leave intake, EDI reconciliation, and automated reminders before a leave ends.

## Who You Are

- 

You have 6–9+ years of experience in benefits administration, leave administration, or People Operations, with hands-on ownership of US benefits and leave.

- 

You have working knowledge of FMLA and multi-state leave, including state PFML and disability programs, CFRA and PDL, intermittent leave, and leave stacking.

- 

You have hands-on experience running the ADA interactive process and PWFA accommodations, with sound documentation and confidentiality practices.

- 

You have practical knowledge of COBRA, ACA employer reporting, HIPAA privacy for plan data, Section 125 qualifying events, and ERISA administrative requirements.

- 

You have Canadian benefits and leave experience, including group benefits, EI and top-up coordination, Records of Employment, provincial leaves, and the duty to accommodate.

- 

You have experience managing leave TPAs, COBRA administrators, brokers, and carriers, including EDI feed troubleshooting.

- 

You have Workday HCM experience in Benefits and Absence and can execute transactions accurately. This is a Workday user role, not a configuration role.

- 

You are proficient with Google Workspace and Slack.

- 

Federal contractor experience, including Section 503 and VEVRAA self-identification and recordkeeping.

- 

Quebec benefits and leave experience.

- 

CEBS, CBP, or CLMS certification.

- 

Experience in operationally complex environments, such as data centers or mixed corporate and frontline workforces.

Active use of AI tools in day-to-day work, with clear practices for protecting PHI and personal data.

us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

What You’ll Do:

You will own cash accounting across a complex, global banking structure and safeguard the integrity of the cash ledger at scale. You will own the key SOX controls over cash and payments and lead the audit relationship. You will re-architect manual processes into automated, AI-enabled workflows built to scale. And you will partner directly with Treasury and Finance leadership, turning complex banking mechanics into decisions. 

Description of the Team

You will be joining an exceptionally credentialed team drawn from Big 4 practice and public company finance, with IPO experience behind us and deep SOX fluency as our baseline rather than our differentiator. We are builders: we design our own automations and deploy agentic AI against work that should not exist. The culture is strategic and genuinely generous, with colleagues who carry real mastery without ever needing to announce it. If you want to do the most technically ambitious cash work in the market alongside people who will make you better, this is where it happens. 

About the role:

Cash Operations Ownership

- Global Cash Accounting: Own the end-to-end accounting for cash and cash equivalents across a high-volume, multi-bank, multi-currency banking structure, including daily cash activity coding, month-end cash tie-outs, and the integrity of the cash ledger at scale.

- Reconciliations at Scale: Own bank and clearing account reconciliations across a large and growing account population; drive aged and unreconciled items to zero by fixing the upstream process, not by papering over the reconciliation.

- Payments & Disbursements: Partner with AP, Payroll, AR, and Treasury to ensure accurate recording, classification, and cut-off of wires, ACH, card, and FX settlement activity; maintain rigorous hygiene over in-transit and suspense balances.

- Restricted Cash & Debt Service: Account for restricted cash, escrow, collateral, and letter of credit balances; support interest, debt service, and covenant-related cash reporting in partnership with Treasury.

- Statement of Cash Flows Support: Provide the transaction-level data, classification logic, and analysis that underpin the Statement of Cash Flows, including proper operating, investing, and financing treatment of complex activity.

SOX Compliance & Control Environment

- Control Ownership: Own and operate key SOX controls over cash, bank reconciliations, payments, and treasury system interfaces; ensure evidence is complete, timely, and audit-ready by design 

- Narratives & Risk Control Matrices: Design and maintain process narratives and Risk Control Matrices for the cash cycle; proactively identify control gaps as volumes, entities, and banking relationships change, and remediate before they become findings.

- Audit Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors on cash and treasury walkthroughs, sample selections, and substantive testing.

### Preferred:

- Experience advising a high-growth cloud, SaaS, data center, infrastructure, or other technology company.

- Experience with public-company cybersecurity materiality, governance, and disclosure processes.

- Experience advising on ransomware, insider threats, supply-chain incidents, credential compromise, and cloud security events.

## About the role

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Identity and Integrations Products team within Security Products. This team builds and operates foundational capabilities for integrations connecting CoreWeave to the breadth of customer security infrastructure, enterprise identity providers and directory services, cloud-native and on-prem key/secrets management (KMS, HSM), and third-party security platforms such as Wiz, CrowdStrike, and SIEM systems.

The role combines people leadership with strong technical judgment: you will guide architecture and engineering decisions, create clarity in complex problem spaces, and ensure that our services meet the availability, security, interoperability, and operational standards expected of a critical cloud platform. You will work closely with product, security, infrastructure, platform, and customer-facing engineering teams.

The ideal candidate has led teams building distributed systems and security-sensitive services and is energized by solving hard problems at the intersection of identity, platform infrastructure, and customer trust.

## What you will do

- Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing Identity and Integrations Products engineering team, including hiring, career development, performance management, and team health.

- Set the team’s technical vision, roadmap, priorities, and execution strategy in partnership with Product Managers and Security Products leadership.

- Own service reliability and operational excellence, including availability, latency, incident response, change management, capacity planning, and continuous improvement.

- Establish engineering practices for secure development, architecture reviews, operational readiness, and sustainable delivery.

- Drive effective cross-functional collaboration across security, infrastructure, networking, developer platform, cloud operations, product, and customer engineering teams.

- Partner with Product Managers, customer-facing engineering teams and customers to understand integration requirements, guide technical discovery, plan rollouts, and resolve complex integration issues.

- Communicate technical decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and progress clearly to engineering, product, security, and executive stakeholders.

## What you bring

- 5+ years of experience managing a complex function or multiple related teams led by manager / tech-leads, including responsibility for strategy, execution, staffing, and engineering quality.

- Experience running engineering operations (observability, SLOs, incident management, post-incident review, capacity planning, release safety) for high-scale services with 99.95%+ availability, 10K RPS or greater.

- Demonstrated ability to make sound technical decisions in ambiguous environments and translate long-term strategy into pragmatic execution.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence across organizational boundaries and work with external customers or partners.

- A track record of delivering through ambiguity and aligning Product, Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure stakeholders.

- Willingness to work on-site in Sunnyvale, California. This role is not remote.

## Preferred qualifications

- Experience building security products or platforms for enterprise, regulated, or security-sensitive customers.

- Experience with identity, key management, encryption, secrets management, confidential computing, or security integrations.

- Experience partnering with external customers, technology partners, or security reviewers on product requirements and assurance.

- Experience leading greenfield products from early architecture through production adoption.

## How you will be successful

In your first year, you will:

- Build trust with the Identity and Integrations Products team and key partner organizations.

- Establish a clear technical and execution roadmap aligned with Security Products and CoreWeave priorities.

- Improve the reliability, observability, and operational maturity of the team’s most critical services.

- Raise the quality and consistency of architecture, security, and operational reviews.

- Hire and develop exceptional engineers while creating a healthy, accountable, and high-performing team culture.

## Why join Security Products

Security Products is building the systems that make CoreWeave trustworthy at scale. You will have the opportunity to lead a team responsible for foundational capabilities that protect access to cloud resources, enable secure product experiences, and support customers running critical AI workloads.

This is a high-impact leadership role for an engineering manager who wants to shape both the technology and the organization behind a modern cloud security platform.
