## About Security Products

The Security Products organization builds the identity, authorization, cryptography, key management, and trust capabilities that help customers securely run sensitive workloads on CoreWeave. We work across product and infrastructure boundaries to deliver security-critical services that are dependable, standards-based, and simple to use.

## About the role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and operate scalable, reliable web services in a distributed-systems environment. You will work on foundational security products and services that protect customer data, enforce access decisions, and provide trustworthy building blocks for the CoreWeave platform.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex backend problems end to end, from API and service design through implementation, testing, deployment, observability, and production operations. You will work closely with engineers, product managers, security specialists, and infrastructure teams to turn ambiguous requirements into secure, maintainable systems.

The ideal candidate combines strong software-engineering fundamentals with sound judgment around reliability, security boundaries, failure modes, and operational trade-offs. You will also help integrate CoreWeave security services with customers’ on-premises and cloud environments, including the identity, key-management, and security products they already use. You will have meaningful ownership of technical direction and delivery while helping raise the engineering bar across the team.

## What you’ll do

- Design and implement scalable, reliable backend services using REST and/or gRPC APIs.

- Define clear API contracts, service boundaries, data models, and integration patterns.

- Own services through their full lifecycle: architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, observability, on-call support, and continuous improvement.

- Improve service reliability through effective error handling, retries, timeouts, idempotency, back-pressure, capacity planning, and graceful degradation.

- Establish and use service observability, including metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and actionable alerts to understand system health and customer impact.

- Participate in design reviews, code reviews, incident response, and post-incident improvements.

- Collaborate with Product, Security Engineering, Infrastructure, and partner teams to deliver secure and usable platform capabilities.

- Design and support integrations with customers’ on-premises and cloud environments and with their security products, such as identity providers, key-management services, HSMs, SIEMs, and policy or access-control systems.

- Work with customers and internal stakeholders to understand integration constraints, define reliable contracts, and guide secure adoption across heterogeneous environments.

- Make pragmatic trade-offs between near-term delivery, long-term maintainability, performance, and operational risk.

- Mentor engineers and contribute to a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous learning.

## What you’ll bring

- Strong professional experience building and operating production backend services and improving their reliability, performance, and maintainability..

- Experience designing and implementing RESTful and/or gRPC APIs.

- Deep understanding of distributed-systems principles, including consistency, concurrency, fault tolerance, networking, and service-to-service communication.

- Fluency in Go, Java, C++ or Python; willingness to work primarily in Go.

- Experience with relational or distributed data stores, asynchronous processing, and service integration patterns.

- Strong testing practices, including unit, integration, contract, load, and failure-mode testing as appropriate.

- Ability to communicate technical decisions clearly in design documents, reviews, and cross-functional discussions.

- Sound judgment when working with sensitive data, trust boundaries, authorization decisions, and security-sensitive failure modes.

## Preferred qualifications

Experience in one or more of the following areas is helpful but not required:

- Designing or building authorization systems at scale, including policy evaluation, permissions, tenant isolation, or least-privilege access.

- Encryption, key management systems, cloud key management services, HSMs, or KMIP.

- OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, workload identity, federation, or related identity protocols.

- SCIM, enterprise identity integrations, SSO, or lifecycle management.

- SRE and reliability practices, including incident response, error budgets, capacity planning, and operational readiness.

- Service observability using metrics, structured logging, distributed tracing, and production diagnostics.

- Load testing, performance analysis, capacity modeling, and scaling strategy.

- Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, or platform engineering.

- Building security products for enterprise, regulated, or otherwise security-sensitive customers.

- Integrating SaaS or cloud services with customer-managed on-premises infrastructure, private clouds, public clouds, and enterprise security products.

## What success looks like

In your first three months, you will develop a deep understanding of the team’s systems and customers, and contribute to production services. You will take ownership of meaningful technical problems and improve the clarity, reliability, and operational readiness of the services you support.

Over time, you will deliver secure and dependable capabilities, influence architecture beyond your immediate area, improve API and service reliability, and help the team scale its engineering practices as the Security Products portfolio grows.

## Why join Security Products?

- Build foundational security capabilities for an AI-native cloud platform.

- Solve challenging problems at the intersection of security, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and customer experience.

- Work on services where correctness, reliability, and thoughtful security design matter every day.

- Partner with experienced engineers, product leaders, and security specialists across CoreWeave.

- Have a direct impact on the trust and adoption of the CoreWeave platform.

## About the role

CoreWeave is looking for a Senior Talent Sourcer (Contract) to help drive high-impact hiring across several of the company’s most important and fast-moving organizations. This person will support executive and senior-level talent work across Operations and IT, Revenue and GTM, and select G&A and Marketing functions. The role is especially aligned to complex, business-critical hiring tied to infrastructure, operations, and commercial scale.

This is not a narrow top-of-funnel sourcer role. We are looking for someone who operates as a hybrid of sourcer, researcher, and talent partner — someone who can build and maintain executive-level pipelines, generate market intelligence, create real momentum on hard searches, and step in wherever needed to help move a search forward.

The ideal person is highly organized, deeply research-oriented, strong with executive-level candidate messaging, fluent in modern AI sourcing and outreach tools, and comfortable engaging directly with senior stakeholders. This person should bring sharp market instincts, excellent follow-through, and the ability to combine automation with the highly personalized approach needed for executive talent. This role is designed around the kind of sourcing motion described in our internal sourcing and sourcer/recruiter operating models: talent mapping, calibration, outreach strategy, executive-grade research, and proactive pipeline building with clear ownership and measurable outcomes.

## Scope and responsibilities

This role will primarily support executive and senior-level searches across several of CoreWeave’s most important functions and should be capable of shifting focus quickly based on business need.

- COO / Operations and IT organizations, including Operations, IT, Supply Chain, Data Center, infrastructure-adjacent hiring, and select international roles

- CIO-aligned IT functions, including networking, infrastructure, systems administration, and related technical operational hiring

- CRO / Revenue and GTM organizations, including sales, revenue, business development, solutions, post-sales, and other commercial functions

- Select engineering-adjacent roles tied to field engineering, solutions engineering, and occasional light software engineering support where needed

- Other significant areas of support include Marketing and G&A (Legal, People Ops, Finance, Procurement, Executive Support)

This person will operate as a hybrid of sourcer, researcher, and talent partner. They will be expected to build and maintain strong, always-on executive pipelines; conduct deep market research and talent mapping; identify target companies and adjacent talent pools; and create executive-grade candidate lists, market briefs, and search insights that help shape strategy.

They should be excellent at highly personalized outreach and candidate messaging, with the ability to attract hard-to-reach executive talent using a mix of automation, research, creativity, and strong follow-up. This person should be comfortable using modern AI sourcing and outreach tools, tracking outreach analytics and funnel health, and adjusting strategy based on real-time conversion data and market signal.

The role also requires strong partnership with recruiters and hiring leaders. This includes attending intake, calibration, and stakeholder meetings; contributing informed market perspective; conducting initial candidate conversations as needed; helping qualify early interest; and moving candidates forward by coordinating hiring manager and panel interviews before handing off to the recruiter at the appropriate stage. This person should be ready to clear roadblocks, keep multiple high-priority searches moving, and act as a strong market-facing representative of the talent function.

## What we’re looking for

- Significant experience in talent sourcing, executive sourcing, recruiting research, talent intelligence, executive search, or a closely related recruiting function

- Strong track record supporting executive or senior-level hiring across multiple major functional areas, ideally spanning some combination of Operations, IT, Supply Chain, Data Center, Revenue, GTM, G&A, or Marketing

- Deep research capability — someone who is not just generating names, but producing usable insight, market perspective, and search direction

- Excellent executive-level messaging instincts and the ability to engage difficult-to-reach talent with credibility and personalization

- Strong sourcing judgment across multiple channels, including LinkedIn, referrals, CRM/ATS rediscovery, adjacent market mapping, and non-obvious talent paths

- High comfort level with modern AI sourcing, research, and outreach tools, and the judgment to use them well

- Strong data and analytics orientation, including comfort using outreach metrics, funnel insights, and search diagnostics to adjust strategy

- Strong understanding of leveling and talent calibration, especially in large-scale tech environments

- Executive presence and confidence in meetings with senior stakeholders

- Very strong organization and follow-through, with the ability to juggle a high volume of requirements at once, stay on top of many moving pieces, and not drop the ball in a fast-paced environment

- A highly proactive operating style — someone who sees gaps, clears blockers, and pushes work forward without waiting to be told

- Strong market instincts, including knowing which companies tend to produce strong talent for specific functions, levels, and environments

- A strong existing network in relevant talent markets is highly desirable

- Experience supporting executive or highly strategic searches in high-growth technology, infrastructure, cloud, hyperscaler, data center, or AI-related environments is strongly preferred

- Experience supporting searches that combine operational scale with technical complexity is strongly preferred

- Familiarity with Business, Operations, IT, and GTM talent markets at companies with strong leveling discipline and mature hiring systems is preferred

- Experience operating in fast-moving environments where priorities can shift quickly and searches require both rigor and creativity is preferred

- Experience supporting international hiring, global market mapping, or contractor/FTE blended talent strategies is a plus

## How this role should operate

The right person for this role will behave like a high-leverage talent partner, not just a requisition helper. They should be capable of building a search strategy, pressure-testing assumptions, producing meaningful research, creating a strong candidate narrative, and driving sustained top-of-funnel momentum at all times. Internally, this should look much closer to a strategic sourcer/researcher model than a traditional transactional sourcing motion — the kind of work where market intelligence, tooling fluency, search discipline, and executive communication all matter together.

You’ll collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, external vendors, and key stakeholders to deliver performant, reliable, and scalable hardware solutions that power CoreWeave’s rapidly growing infrastructure.

You will own server hardware from provisioning through decommission. This hands-on role combines engineering and operational support. Engineering work includes automation across the hardware lifecycle, hardware and firmware management services, monitoring and alerting, and qualification and bring-up of new platforms. Operational support includes acting as a senior point of contact for hardware escalations, driving deep root-cause analysis across hardware and firmware, and working quality and RMA issues through to resolution with server vendors and OEMs.

Both engineering and operational support are core responsibilities. You will support the systems you build and use what you learn from production failures to improve automation, telemetry, and platform design. You will work closely with data center operations teams, hardware technicians, and engineering teams to bring new regions online and keep existing infrastructure healthy.

## What You’ll Do

- Design and develop server hardware infrastructure to support CoreWeave’s high-performance workloads.

- Automate all aspects of the server hardware lifecycle, from provisioning and configuration through firmware management, monitoring, and decommissioning.

- Develop and maintain hardware and firmware management services that ensure reliability at scale.

- Develop and implement monitoring and alerting for server hardware health, improving alert quality to support reliable on-call response.

- Serve as a senior point of contact for hardware escalations, performing deep troubleshooting and root-cause analysis across hardware and firmware to drive long-term fixes.

- Participate in an on-call rotation for hardware escalations and improve the runbooks, alerts, and tooling that make the rotation sustainable.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define hardware requirements, specifications, and system architecture.

- Work with server vendors and OEMs to evaluate, qualify, and deploy new platforms and resolve firmware, quality, and RMA issues.

- Support new data center region bring-up and hardware qualification.

- Analyze hardware system performance, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to efficiency and resilience.

- Establish and continuously refine processes for internal hardware testing, deployment, and performance optimization.

- Create and maintain accurate documentation of hardware designs, specifications, test procedures, and results.

- Support data center operations teams and hardware technicians with troubleshooting guidance, runbooks, and training so common issues can be resolved without engineering escalation.

- Turn recurring production failures into automation, better telemetry, and improvements to platform design and vendor solutions.

- Communicate status, trade-offs, and risks clearly to engineering, operations, and customer-facing stakeholders, including during active incidents.

- 4 years working w/ server hardware, components, and management technologies.

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field

- Proficiency in Ansible or Python, with hands-on experience programmatically interacting with server BMCs using Redfish or IPMI; Redfish preferred.

- Experience collaborating with hardware vendors and OEMs to evaluate, qualify, and deploy server solutions.

- Demonstrated experience supporting and troubleshooting production infrastructure, participating in on-call or escalation rotations, and driving incidents through to root-cause resolution.

- Comfort with both building and automating systems and supporting infrastructure already in production.

- Proven ability to stay current with technologies and trends in server and data center hardware.

- Strong interest in automation and infrastructure scalability, with a commitment to continuous improvement.

- Excellent technical documentation skills and attention to detail.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a bias toward systematic, data-driven decisions.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to work effectively with technical teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Experience bringing up new data center regions or standing up infrastructure in a new geography.

- Experience with GPU platforms and rack-scale systems such as NVIDIA GB200 or GB300.

- Experience with BMC technologies and management interfaces such as Redfish or IPMI at fleet scale.

- Experience with firmware lifecycle management or hardware qualification programs in large-scale environments.

- Strong Linux systems administration and debugging skills at fleet scale.

- Familiarity with Kubernetes-based services, observability tools such as Prometheus and Grafana, and distributed production environments.

- Experience designing alerting, runbooks, and self-service tooling that enable operations teams to resolve common hardware failures without engineering escalation.

- Experience supporting external customers or partners in a technical troubleshooting capacity.

us.location: New York, NY / Sunnyvale, CA / Bellevue, WA
us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

### What You'll Do:

As Senior Product Marketing Manager for AI Training Infrastructure, you will own CoreWeave's AI Training Infrastructure story, all aspects of building and training a model, and partner on all post-training and optimization launches and narratives.

The role is not organized around a product list. It is organized around what research and platform teams are actually trying to accomplish at this stage, and the infrastructure decisions that either let them move fast or slow them down. SUNK is the most differentiated expression of CoreWeave's answer to that problem, the product in this scope with the deepest operational proof at scale. The broader story spans CoreWeave Kubernetes Service and a growing Kubernetes-native training surface expanding independently of Slurm. That includes understanding where open source frameworks like Ray, SkyPilot, and Kueue fit in the conversation, where community debate is shaping buyer expectations, and how ecosystem partnerships factor into how teams evaluate and adopt training infrastructure.

You are not inheriting four separate product stories and stitching them together. You are building the connective narrative across CoreWeave's training stack and the broader ML ecosystem it connects to, including the experiment tracking workflows, open source tooling, and practitioner communities that researchers already operate in. CoreWeave's integration with Weights and Biases connects infrastructure signals to the experiment tracking tools researchers already use. Part of this role is understanding how that integration shapes researcher perception of CoreWeave and building messaging around it. That means translating capabilities across the stack, topology-aware scheduling, bare-metal performance, Kubernetes-native lifecycle management, automated cluster health management, into messaging that resonates with AI research leaders, platform teams, and the wider ML researcher community beyond the largest labs.

### About the role:

Positioning and messaging

- Own the AI Training Infrastructure narrative for CoreWeave. That narrative is built on real credibility: CoreWeave infrastructure has been used to train many of the most widely used models in production today. Your job is to deepen and expand that story, building the strategic positioning framework that ties CoreWeave Kubernetes Service, SUNK, and SUNK Anywhere into a coherent market story, deciding how each product is positioned relative to the others, and ensuring that framework holds across every customer-facing surface.

- Shape how CoreWeave competes in training-focused sales situations. That means owning the competitive positioning framework field teams use against alternative infrastructure approaches, the persona-specific messaging that translates infrastructure capabilities into outcomes research leaders and platform teams care about, and the launch narrative for new capabilities as they reach the market.

Customer proof

- Own the customer evidence strategy for AI Training Infrastructure. Decide which proof points matter for which buyers at which stage. Build the feedback loops that surface deployment insight from Solutions Architects and customer-facing engineers. Ensure that evidence reaches assets without losing specificity in translation. The goal is a proof strategy that makes every customer-facing asset more credible, not a library of case studies.

GTM and sales enablement

- Define how CoreWeave's training stack goes to market. Own the enablement framework for Sales and Solutions Architects. Set the competitive positioning strategy the field uses in training-focused deals. Partner with DevRel on content and enablement for technical audiences, including developers, researchers, and community contributors. That boundary requires active coordination and will evolve as both roles do. Partner with CoreWeave's technical and applied ML teams on benchmarking and performance validation that supports how the training stack is positioned and evaluated in market.

Metrics and measurement

- Define how product marketing's impact is measured for AI Training Infrastructure, not just whether assets were delivered. Own the metrics that matter: deal velocity, contract value, competitive win rates in training-related opportunities, and platform adoption and retention. Use that data to make the case internally for where AI Training Infrastructure messaging is moving deals and where it needs to change.

### Who You Are:

- 5+ years in product marketing, technical marketing, or GTM, in cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, or developer tooling.

- Working fluency with Kubernetes. You do not need to have operated clusters, but you need to understand how teams use them and why the infrastructure decisions around them matter.

- Direct experience with or proximity to AI researchers: how they think, what they evaluate, what earns trust versus eye-rolls.

- Familiarity with the AI model development lifecycle from pre-training through fine-tuning, RL, and optimization. You know what this stage of the workflow costs teams when it breaks down.

- Demonstrated ability to build positioning and messaging for complex technical products that moved something, adoption, market perception, or competitive win rate. Not just produced, shipped.

- Sound judgment inside ambiguity. You have worked in a fast-moving org where role definitions shifted and used that as information, not a blocker.

### Preferred:

- Experience marketing platform or infrastructure products where the buyer is a platform engineer, research lead, or technical architect.

- Familiarity with schedulers, clusters, or distributed training workloads, Slurm, Kubernetes-native training, or both.

- Track record across multiple products or a portfolio simultaneously, not a single-product PMM motion.

- Background in developer tools, HPC, or AI infrastructure. You have marketed highly technical products to audiences who evaluate claims on technical merit, not positioning.

### Wondering if you're a good fit?

We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. 

### Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

- Be Curious at Your Core

- Act Like an Owner

- Empower Employees

- Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences

- Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for take off, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

us.location: Livingston, NJ / New York, NY / Sunnyvale, CA / Bellevue, WA
us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

## Role Overview

CoreWeave is seeking an experienced Network Security Engineer for our network security initiatives to help protect our rapidly scaling cloud infrastructure hosting high-performance AI workloads. In this role, you will architect and implement cutting-edge security solutions focused on network security across our data center perimeter and internal networks. You will work in a high-scale environment (CoreWeave is positioning itself as the next major hyperscaler) and ensure our network and services remain secure, resilient, and trustworthy. The ideal candidate is a seasoned security expert (3–7 years experience) with a deep understanding of modern cloud/network architectures and a passion for educating cross-functional partners in a security-first culture.

## Key Responsibilities

- Network Security Architecture: Design and deploy robust security measures across the network perimeter and internal fabrics (e.g., firewalls, IPS/IDS, segmentation, configuration health, best practicies) to protect CoreWeave’s globally distributed hyperscale infrastructure hosting large-scale AI workloads. Ensure that all entry points, high-speed interconnects, and cloud services are fortified against unauthorized access and attacks.

- Zero Trust Implementation: Champion a Zero Trust security model across CoreWeave’s network and cloud environments. Architect solutions that enforce least-privilege access, continuous verification, and micro-segmentation of services – ensuring no implicit trust at any layer.

- Security Monitoring & Incident Response: Establish robust monitoring for network security events and potential breaches across high-density AI cluster networks. Proactively identify vulnerabilities or indicators of compromise, and coordinate incident response efforts for any network-related security incidents to minimize impact.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Networking, Infrastructure, and Software Engineering teams to integrate security best practices into architecture, deployments, and processes. Provide expert guidance during design and code reviews to ensure new services and features are secure by design.

us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About this role

We're looking for a Senior Engineer to be a driving force on CoreWeave's Benchmarking & Performance team, with a focus on building the performance insights and observability systems that make our AI infrastructure legible at every layer, from individual GPUs and NVLink/InfiniBand fabrics up through distributed training and inference workloads. You will own how we detect, diagnose, and surface performance signals across every data center in our global infrastructure, turning billions of raw telemetry events into real-time insight that engineers, product teams, and executives can act on with confidence.

This is not a straightforward data engineering or BI role. The role will focus on building the observability and insight tooling that lets us answer, in near real time, whether a GPU fleet, a fabric, or a training run is performing the way it should, and why it isn't when it's not. If you're energized by building the systems that turn raw infrastructure telemetry into trusted, actionable performance intelligence, and you want that work to sit closer to the hardware and the workload than to a dashboard, this role was built for you.

What you'll do

- Performance Insights & Observability - Design and build the systems that continuously assess AI infrastructure health and performance: GPU utilization and efficiency, interconnect (NVLink, InfiniBand, RoCE) fabric behavior, distributed training and inference throughput, and hardware degradation signals. Build the detection and diagnosis logic that surfaces anomalies and regressions before they become incidents, not just dashboards that report on them after the fact.

- Time-Series & Metrics Infrastructure - Own and extend our time-series database (TSDB) layer as the backbone of real-time observability. Write and optimize PromQL/MetricsQL queries that power alerting, anomaly detection, and trend analysis across thousands of GPUs and hundreds of benchmark runs. Bridge streaming metrics and batch-analytical workloads so engineers get sub-second answers during live incidents and analysts get complete historical context for root cause work.

- Fabric & GPU Telemetry - Build and validate the pipelines and metrics that make network fabric and GPU-level behavior observable and comparable across racks, clusters, and hardware generations, including gray failure detection, congestion and error-rate signals, and health scoring that holds up under audit.

- Data Lake Architecture (in support of insight work) - Design and build the performance data lake that underpins the above: table formats (Apache Iceberg, Parquet, Avro), hot/cold tiering, and schema evolution for latency distributions, throughput metrics, GPU utilization, cost-per-token, and hardware health signals. This is foundational infrastructure, not the end product.

- Query Optimization & Performance - Profile and tune query engines against columnar and time-series stores so that the observability layer meets its own strict P99 latency and freshness SLAs. Benchmark the benchmarking infrastructure itself.

- BI & Reporting (secondary) - Where needed, build self-service views (Grafana, Looker, or similar) for engineers, product managers, and executives, but as a downstream output of the insight and observability work above, not the primary deliverable.

Who you are

- 5+ years of experience building distributed systems, observability platforms, or performance engineering tooling, ideally for infrastructure or ML systems rather than general-purpose BI.

- Strong coding in Python or Go (C++ a plus) and deep familiarity with networked systems, GPU infrastructure, and performance analysis.

- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes at production scale, CI/CD, and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) used to monitor and diagnose infrastructure, not just report on it.

- Working knowledge of time-series databases and fluency in PromQL or MetricsQL for building real-time alerting and anomaly detection, not only historical dashboards.

- Familiarity with data lake architectures and modern table formats (Iceberg, Parquet, Avro) sufficient to support an insights platform, though this is not the primary skill this role is hiring for.

- Comfortable working close to hardware and workload behavior: GPU utilization patterns, interconnect fabric health, distributed training/inference performance characteristics.

- Strong communicator comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams and external partners.

Nice to have

- Experience with time-series databases, LSM-based storage engines, or custom telemetry pipelines.

- Experience running MLPerf submissions or similar large-scale audited benchmarks.

- Contributions to OSS projects such as Apache Iceberg, Apache Spark, Trino, llm-d, vLLM, or PyTorch.

- Direct experience benchmarking or monitoring large GPU fleets or multi-region clusters.

- Experience with CUDA kernels, NCCL/SHARP, RDMA/NUMA, or GPU interconnect topologies.

- Familiarity with data cataloging, lineage tools, or data governance frameworks.

Why CoreWeave?

Own the data that tells the truth about performance. You'll build the analytical foundations the industry relies on to measure—and achieve—state-of-the-art results, working hand-in-hand with world-class partners and communities. If you love turning vast streams of telemetry into clear, trusted insights that move markets and drive engineering excellence, we'd love to talk.

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

- Be Curious at Your Core

- Act Like an Owner

- Empower Employees

- Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences

- Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for take off, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

Your work will focus on turning complex, multi-step operational procedures into simple, safe, and auditable automation for internal users operating at hyperscale.

- Strong understanding of Linux systems and how to debug issues across processes, networking, and storage.

- Experience with Kubernetes or similar container orchestration platforms and their APIs (for example, interacting with custom resources, controllers, or operators).

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred:

- Experience designing and operating services that automate lifecycle management for large fleets of physical servers or other hardware.

- Experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management tools (for example, Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or Salt).

CoreWeave runs some of the largest GPU clusters in the world, and the network has a lot to do with how well they perform. - Diagnosing distributed failures across hundreds of nodes, such as ECMP blackholing across fabric planes.

# What You'll Do:

The Cloud Platform API team builds the platform and infrastructure that front CoreWeave's control plane. This role sits with the group that owns the API Gateway (the single secure front door for control-plane traffic) and the Kubernetes Gateway, one secure endpoint into every CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) cluster control plane, public or private. The team runs the Envoy and Kubernetes Gateway API stack that carries every customer, CLI, console, and Terraform request. This is high-leverage infrastructure at CoreWeave: the gateway is the choke point, and its latency and availability are what customers perceive as the platform's.

# About the Role:

As a Senior Engineer on the Cloud Platform API team, you'll design and operate the gateways that front the entire control plane. You'll drive large-scale networking migrations, such as moving from NGINX/HAProxy to Envoy across every zone with no customer-visible regression, and own routing, TLS/mTLS, rate limiting, and observability across the stack. You'll set technical direction for how the team runs its infrastructure, anticipate problems before they turn into incidents, and help stand up new customer-facing features for this infra. You'll also mentor other engineers, lead post-mortems, and act as a trusted advisor across teams like CKS, VPC, IAM, Cloud Console, and more. This role sits on a technical-leadership track, and we especially welcome engineers interested in eventually leading or managing a team.

- Own the API and Kubernetes Gateways API stacks and their CRDs: routing, TLS/mTLS, rate limiting, and observability.

- Drive large-scale infrastructure migrations (for example, HAProxy → Envoy) across every zone with one audit-log shape and no customer-visible regression.

You own the deal from first conversation through execution, and you make the broader field organization smarter and faster at every stage of that process.

About the role: As a Principal Solution Specialist for Infrastructure, you design the frameworks that govern how CoreWeave structures large infrastructure commitments, negotiate the commercial terms that create durable value for both sides, and build the playbooks and processes the field team relies on to win. But this role goes beyond deal mechanics: you will develop an instinctive understanding of what AI companies need to build across every layer of the infrastructure stack, and across every stage of company maturity from early-stage startup to hyperscale enterprise. In a market changing as fast as AI infrastructure, the intelligence you gather from customer conversations feeds directly into CoreWeave's product, engineering, capacity planning, finance, and marketing teams. This role sits at the intersection of sales, operations, enablement, and deal desk, and the insight it generates shapes how CoreWeave builds and goes to market.

In this role, you will:

- Own the end-to-end commercial and operational lifecycle of CoreWeave's most complex infrastructure deals globally, from initial deal architecture through term negotiation, contract execution, and account expansion.

- Structure and close large-scale infrastructure commitments, from long-term compute and networking agreements to fully integrated AI platform deals, in close coordination with sales, legal, finance, and product teams across CoreWeave.

- Design deal frameworks, pricing models, and term structures that reflect what AI companies actually need to build at scale, balancing customer requirements around resource access, cost predictability, and operational flexibility with CoreWeave's commercial objectives.

- Own the deal desk function for infrastructure commitments, providing real-time deal guidance, commercial structuring support, and pricing alignment to the field team across active opportunities globally.

- Enable the sales and solutions architecture organizations with infrastructure deal playbooks, term negotiation frameworks, TCO models, and competitive positioning materials that accelerate large infrastructure closings.

- Engage directly with customer procurement, legal, and executive leadership as CoreWeave's primary commercial voice in complex, multi-stakeholder infrastructure negotiations.

- Partner with product specialists across Core Services, AI Runtime, AI Developer Services, and Data Services to build integrated deal proposals that reflect the full value of CoreWeave's infrastructure platform.

- Serve as the field's primary intelligence source on how AI companies across industries and company stages think about and consume infrastructure, translating customer conversations into direct input for CoreWeave's product, engineering, capacity planning, finance, and marketing teams.

- Drive operational improvements in how CoreWeave manages large infrastructure deal cycles, including pipeline visibility, deal review cadences, escalation paths, and post-signature execution handoffs, to support a growing global field organization.

## Who You Are:

- 10+ years of experience in enterprise infrastructure sales, deal structuring, or commercial operations at a cloud provider, hyperscaler, data center operator, or large-scale technology vendor, with a track record of closing large, complex deals.

- 5+ years owning or shaping the commercial structure of large infrastructure commitments, including cloud compute agreements, GPU infrastructure contracts, data center agreements, or equivalent, spanning term negotiation, pricing strategy, and contract execution in a customer-facing capacity.

- Deep understanding of how AI companies, from startups building their first production systems to enterprises scaling global AI deployments, evaluate, procure, and operationalize infrastructure, including the technical, financial, and organizational dynamics that drive those decisions across industries.

- Fluency across CoreWeave's infrastructure portfolio, GPU compute, high-performance networking, storage, and Kubernetes platform, and strong working knowledge of how these components combine into integrated infrastructure commitments for AI customers.

- Proven ability to drive alignment across sales, operations, finance, and legal in a deal structuring capacity, managing complex internal stakeholder environments without losing momentum or commercial clarity.

- Track record of engaging at the executive level with customers, C-suite, VP-level procurement, and legal leadership, across complex, multi-stakeholder commercial negotiations involving significant contract values.

- Commercial fluency across deal structures: long-term commitment economics, ramp schedules, SLA frameworks, and the financial tradeoffs that shape large infrastructure agreements for AI companies at every stage of maturity.

## Preferred:

- Prior experience in a deal desk, commercial operations, or strategic deals function at a cloud provider or hyperscaler (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle Cloud, or equivalent).

- Background in AI infrastructure procurement or sales, with direct experience structuring GPU infrastructure agreements, HPC contracts, or large-scale cloud commitments for AI/ML workloads.

- Experience building and scaling deal processes, including playbooks, approval workflows, and pricing frameworks, that enable a distributed field organization to operate consistently on large, complex deals.

- Advanced degree in Business, Finance, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience with a demonstrated ability to operate at the intersection of commercial strategy, technical infrastructure, and operational execution.

Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk.

- You love sitting at the center of complex deals: you are energized by multi-workstream negotiations where legal, finance, product, and engineering are all in the room and something significant has to close.

- You love acting as the bridge: between the field team's customer commitments and the internal commercial, operational, and financial machinery that makes those commitments real, and you hold both sides accountable.

- You are an expert at navigating "The Room": you have a proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder commercial negotiations on both sides of the table, without losing momentum, clarity, or trust.

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. The Sr. Data Center Design Manager will ensure that all designs align with our project requirements and are executed to meet performance, efficiency, and scalability standards. Acting as the primary point of contact for design-related matters, on a per-project basis, this individual will collaborate with internal teams and external consultants to ensure designs are executed consistently and to the highest quality standards.

25% travel required to various data center sites.

In this role, you will:

- Project Leadership & Oversight: Manage the design and coordination of multiple data center projects concurrently, from concept through detailed design, including Greenfield construction projects, tenant fitouts, build-to-suit projects in existing facilities, renovation projects, equipment upgrades, and end-of-life replacements. Oversee the work of Professional Consultants (Architects, Engineers) and Equipment Suppliers during the design process.

- Single Point of Contact for Design on Assigned Projects: Act as the primary point of contact for all design-related items for assigned projects, coordinating closely with Data Center Providers and their Contractors, Architects/Engineers (A/E firms), along with our internal stakeholders to ensure seamless communication and alignment throughout the design process.

- Internal Coordination with SMEs: Coordinate with internal Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across various disciplines, including electrical, mechanical, LV/IT, and BMS, to ensure project requirements, technical specifications, and solutions are properly aligned, integrating specialized expertise into the design process as needed.

- Standards & Compliance: Apply CoreWeave Design & Engineering Guidelines and industry best practices to ensure alignment with company objectives and emphasize value engineering for optimal cost and performance.

- Managing Basis of Design Deviations: Track and document any deviations from the Basis of Design throughout the project lifecycle, coordinating with internal teams and external consultants.

- Budget & Schedule Coordination: Work with the Construction Management team to prepare, review, and monitor project schedules, budgets, and forecasts for design and construction expenditures.

- OFCI Equipment Management: Review and evaluate OFCI (Owner-Furnished, Contractor-Installed) equipment submittals, providing recommendations to the Construction Management team and Procurement teams.

- Design Reviews: Participate in page-turn meetings with consultants, providing feedback on designs, Sequence of Operations, Basis of Design documents, commissioning plans, and testing scripts.

- Vendor Management: Assist with RFPs for A/E consultants and commissioning agents, evaluation of proposals, selection of vendors, and oversight on alignment with project budgets and schedules, while reviewing/approving consultant invoices.

- Executive & Project Reporting: Prepare and deliver detailed project reports to both executive leadership and project teams, track project budgets, schedules, scope objectives, and progress, ensuring alignment with CoreWeave’s gating process and smooth handoff to the Construction Management team for ongoing management.

- Stakeholder Communication: Provide regular project updates to internal and external stakeholders, both informally and formally.

- Design Coordination & Site Visits: Conduct site visits during construction to review design implementation, assess construction progress, and ensure adherence to design specifications, quality standards, and project requirements.

- Collaboration Across Teams: Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including Capacity, Network Engineering, Construction, Operations, Supply Chain and Technical Project Management to ensure alignment with business objectives and project deliverables. Serve as a liaison between internal teams and external consultants or vendors, ensuring clear and effective communication.

- Innovation & Design Enhancement: Contribute to internal design team meetings, proposing and exploring new technologies or design concepts to enhance project outcomes. Stay up to date with industry trends and integrate innovative solutions into project designs.

- Strong knowledge of data center infrastructure systems, including cooling systems (air-cooled chiller plants, water-cooled chiller plants, liquid cooling), power distribution, UPS systems, generators, familiarity with Building Management/Automation Systems (BMS), and an understanding of LV/IT design.

- Experience with large-scale, high-density data centers and cloud infrastructure, including familiarity with power, cooling, and other critical infrastructure systems.

- Proven ability to manage complex projects with strong project management and organizational skills, ensuring successful project delivery on time and within budget.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, managing multiple projects and competing priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail.

The Business Systems team at CoreWeave partners across Infrastructure, Data Center Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to build and scale the systems that power our global data center footprint. We own the architecture, integrations, and data models that enable accurate tracking and lifecycle management of infrastructure assets across high-growth, high-volume environments. We build our platforms rather than just configure them, giving the company a live, trustworthy model of every data center asset, from the power chain to the rack.

### About the role

In this role, you will build the software, data models, and integrations that connect physical infrastructure (power, cooling, and compute) to the business systems that plan, deploy, and track it. You will design and maintain integrations between upstream Supply Chain systems and downstream Data Center platforms, ensuring an accurate, real-time representation of infrastructure assets. - Drive system standardization and consolidation to support high-volume assembly and deployment operations

- Define and manage the Data Center Systems roadmap, prioritizing scalability, reliability, clarity and consistency of asset data

- Strong understanding of asset hierarchy modeling and infrastructure topology mapping, including power chain, single-line (one-line) diagrams, and failure domains

- Experience building and maintaining integrations between inventory, logistics, and Data Center platforms (DCIM, CMDB, etc.)

- Enable capabilities for asset capacity planning, inbound visibility, receiving readiness, deployment readiness, and lifecycle tracking

- Experience supporting global or multi-site data center environments

## Preferred

- Familiarity with industrial and data center protocols such as Modbus, MQTT, SNMP, Redfish, or BACnet

- Experience with Kubernetes, containerized deployments, or infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform)

- Experience with graph data models, digital-twin representations, or time-series databases

us.title: Staff Product Manager, Training Infrastructure - Weights & Biases

us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About the Role

Training a frontier model is as much an infrastructure problem as it is a modeling problem. When a run fails at hour 47 of a 72-hour job, the question is almost never "what's wrong with the code" — it's "what happened on the cluster." Node failures, network timeouts, storage bottlenecks, and scheduling decisions determine whether training runs succeed or fail, how much they cost, and how fast teams can iterate. Until now, the developer tools and the infrastructure telemetry have lived in completely separate worlds.

The CoreWeave acquisition changes that. W&B can now build products that connect application-level experiment tracking with cluster health, hardware telemetry, and compute orchestration — a surface area that's hard to assemble without owning both the developer tools and the infrastructure.

Reporting to the Director of Product Management, this Staff Product Manager will own the strategy and execution for the products at this intersection: W&B Launch (job submission and compute orchestration), infrastructure insights that leverage CoreWeave's unique telemetry and platform capabilities, and new product concepts — including agentic and automated research workflows — that only exist because W&B and CoreWeave are now one company. Sandboxes (managed development environments) are also part of this surface, but the core opportunity is building infrastructure-native developer tools that take advantage of the combined platform.

You'll be working directly with frontier model builders — teams training on thousands of GPUs — to understand what they need and ship it.

If you're energized by solving infrastructure challenges that directly accelerate deep learning workflows, collaborating with the world’s best AI teams, and delivering tools that move the industry frontier forward, his role is for you.

What You'll Do

- Define and ship infrastructure-native products that only W&B + CoreWeave can build. This is the core of the role. The integration between W&B's experiment tracking and CoreWeave's infrastructure platform opens a new product surface — giving researchers visibility and control that spans their code, their runs, and the machines those runs execute on. You'll identify the highest-value opportunities in this design space, build conviction around them, and drive the roadmap from concept through launch and iteration.

- Own W&B Launch and evolve it for the CoreWeave era. Launch is W&B's job submission and compute orchestration product. Today it helps teams submit training jobs to Kubernetes clusters and cloud providers. As part of a vertically integrated AI platform, Launch can go further — with deeper infrastructure awareness and the ability to serve as the orchestration layer for agentic and automated research workflows. You'll set the vision for what that looks like and ship it.

- Spend real time with frontier AI teams and learn how they actually work. Foundation model builders are your primary customers. You'll spend significant time in their workflows — understanding how they manage infrastructure, debug failures, orchestrate computation, and increasingly automate their research processes. These conversations will directly shape the product roadmap.

- Build the bridge between W&B product and CoreWeave platform engineering. This role sits at the seam between two organizations that are becoming one. You'll partner with CoreWeave's infrastructure and platform teams to identify integration opportunities, and with W&B's engineering teams to build them into products researchers actually want to use. Your ability to translate between infrastructure engineers and ML researchers will be critical.

- Find and resolve friction points in the job submission, compute management, and infrastructure observability workflows, maintaining W&B's high bar for craft and quality.

- Explore new product concepts at the hardware-software boundary. The design space opened by the CoreWeave integration is large — spanning profiling, environments, automation, agents, and more. You'll evaluate which new concepts have the highest impact for frontier AI teams and drive the most promising ones from zero to one.

Who You Are

- Experience: You have 7+ years as a product manager working on developer tools, deep learning infrastructure, or ML engineer platforms.

- End-to-end ownership: You've taken a technical product—whether a model, orchestration feature, or developer tool—all the way to production, including defining success criteria, measuring effectiveness, and iterating to improve impact and user happiness.

- Technical fluency: You’re comfortable discussing Kubernetes and SLURM, job scheduling, hyperparameter optimization algorithms, and API design with engineers and AI researchers.

- Cross-functional influence:  You’re skilled at managing and influencing AI engineers, software engineers, and stakeholders—with or without official authority—to align teams and drive outcomes.

- Clear communication: A major part of this role is seeking feedback from many directions and channeling it into a single, executable stream. You bring clarity and organization to complex, fast-moving environments.

- Care and taste: You have strong opinions about the products you use and a high bar for developer experience.

Preferred

- Experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX), distributed training, or LLM development workflows.

- Hands-on experience with SLURM or Kubernetes for GPU-intensive workloads.

- Prior exposure to W&B or other experiment-tracking and model management platforms.

- Understanding of hyperparameter optimization methods and evaluation workflows for large models.

Wondering if You're a Good Fit?

We believe in investing in our people and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams—even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team:

- Outgoing and user-focused. You'll love this role if you enjoy connecting with real users day to day, helping them solve issues, and sharing patterns for making the most of our products

- Self-directed and willing to take risks. At our speed and scale, product managers need to proactively find solutions, improve processes, and collaborate with team members and engaged users. Your initiative will really shine here.

- Hands-on with AI. You experiment with generative AI to improve your own workflow and build user-facing prototypes.  You keep up to date every day with what’s new in the AI / LLM world.

- Passionate about developer experience. You care deeply about building tools that help AI practitioners accelerate their iteration and discovery.  You know small friction points compound, and smoothing them out is what makes a delightful and winning developer tool.

Why Us?

We work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

us.content:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

### About CoreWeave

CoreWeave is the AI Hyperscaler™, delivering a cloud platform of cutting edge services powering the next wave of AI. Our technology provides enterprises and leading AI labs with the most performant, efficient and resilient solutions for accelerated computing. Since 2017, CoreWeave has operated a growing footprint of data centers covering every region of the US and across Europe. CoreWeave was ranked as one of the TIME100 most influential companies of 2024.

As the leader in the industry, we thrive in an environment where adaptability and resilience are key. Our culture offers career-defining opportunities for those who excel amid change and challenge. If you’re someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, enjoys solving complex problems, and is eager to make a significant impact, CoreWeave is the place for you. Join us, and be part of a team solving some of the most exciting challenges in the industry.  

CoreWeave powers the creation and delivery of the intelligence that drives innovation. 

About the Role

This is a senior individual contributor role with high visibility and cross-functional reach. You will not manage people — you will manage programs, processes, and accountability across an organization that is scaling faster than its existing playbooks.

A core focus of this role is the network backbone and long-haul fiber connectivity that makes each new site usable. Data center capacity is only as valuable as the connectivity that reaches it, and fiber has the longest and least forgiving lead time of any dependency in the expansion pipeline — dark fiber and IRU negotiations, carrier and subsea capacity procurement, permitting and right-of-way, conduit and duct builds, landing station and cable landing point coordination, metro rings, and cross-connects at interconnection facilities. You will own the sequencing of that connectivity workstream against site readiness, ensuring fiber, transport, and interconnect milestones land ahead of power and compute turn-up rather than behind it.

In this role, you will:

- Own and continuously maintain the master interdependency tracker linking the international pipeline to the domestic development pipeline — surface resource conflicts, sequencing risks, and capacity constraints in real time to program leadership.

- Drive cross-functional accountability across Legal, Finance, Engineering, and Operations: track commitments made in program reviews, follow up on open action items, escalate blockers proactively, and ensure teams are moving at the pace the program requires.

- Own the end-to-end program plan for network backbone and fiber connectivity at each new market and site — from route planning and carrier/dark fiber selection through contracting, construction, splicing, acceptance testing, and lit service turn-up — and hold the critical path against data center RFS dates.

- Manage carrier, dark fiber provider, subsea consortium, and construction partner deliverables against schedule, quality, and diversity requirements: route diversity and physical path separation, latency budgets, capacity commitments, SLAs, and IRU/lease terms. Partner with Legal, Finance, and Sourcing to move agreements through negotiation and execution on the program timeline.

- Ensure all active opportunities and programs progress through required intake, review, and approval gates on schedule — flag deviations, at-risk milestones, and sequencing conflicts before they become delays.

- Maintain a connectivity view of the portfolio: fiber route inventory, contracted vs. lit capacity, diversity posture, interconnection footprint, and per-site connectivity readiness — so leadership can see where the backbone constrains growth.

- Engage substantively in technical discussions with network engineering and architecture teams — challenge assumptions on route design, capacity planning, and turn-up sequencing, and contribute to problem-solving rather than only reporting status

- Build and continuously improve the systems that make this function scalable: intake workflows, tracking templates, milestone frameworks, and reporting cadences that hold up as the program portfolio grows across domestic and international markets.

Minimum Qualifications

-  5+ years in technical program management, program operations, or strategic analytics within data center, network infrastructure, telecommunications, or capital-intensive sectors.

- Working knowledge of network backbone and fiber infrastructure — long-haul and metro fiber, dark fiber and IRU structures, DWDM/optical transport, interconnection and colocation cross-connects, route diversity, and the mechanics of a fiber build (permitting, ROW, construction, splicing, OTDR acceptance testing, turn-up).

- Comfortable managing external vendors and partners to schedule, quality, and contractual commitments — carriers, dark fiber providers, construction contractors, or equivalent.

- Solid understanding of hardware development lifecycles.

- Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence without direct authority, and drive consensus in a fast-paced environment.

- Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills.

- Proficiency in program management tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Sheet).

Preferred Qualifications

- Master's degree in Engineering or an MBA.

- 10+ years of experience in technical program management within the hardware industry, with a strong focus on Networking hardware technologies.

- Experience with networking switch designs for both Infiniband and high speed Ethernet.

- Direct experience delivering fiber or network backbone programs: metro/long-haul builds, subsea cable systems or landing stations, carrier capacity procurement, or large-scale interconnection deployments.

- Familiarity with hyperscale or cloud network architectures — DCI, backbone/WAN capacity planning, peering and transit strategy, and how connectivity requirements are derived from compute deployment plans.

- Experience navigating international telecom permitting, licensing, and regulatory regimes, and coordinating with in-country carriers and construction partners.

- Experience working with international manufacturing partners and supply chains.

- Familiarity with industry standards and regulatory compliance for hardware products.

Why CoreWeave

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of growth, scaling at an unprecedented speed. We are frequently challenging the norm, exploring new technologies and advancing the potential for hyperscale. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our products and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

- Be Curious at Your Core

- Act Like an Owner

- Empower Employees

- Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences

- Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we continue to grow, opportunities within the organization are evolving and expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. If this resonates with you, come join us!

The base salary range for this role is $182,000 to $242,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility). 

What We Offer

The range we’ve posted represents the typical compensation range for this role. To determine actual compensation, we review the market rate for each candidate which can include a variety of factors. These include qualifications, experience, interview performance, and location.

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings for full-time employees; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include:

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance - 100% paid for by CoreWeave

- Company-paid Life Insurance 

- Voluntary supplemental life insurance 

- Short and long-term disability insurance 

- Flexible Spending Account

- Health Savings Account

- Tuition Reimbursement 

- Ability to Participate in Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

- Mental Wellness Benefits through Spring Health 

- Family-Forming support provided by Carrot

- Paid Parental Leave 

- Flexible, full-service childcare support with Kinside

- 401(k) with a generous employer match

- Flexible PTO

- Catered lunch each day in our office and data center locations

- A casual work environment

- A work culture focused on innovative disruption
